correctness.rationale: In the closed neighborhood there is a complete column and two distinct lateral vertices (also for n=3). With signs x, summing the row equations gives mS_j+S_(j−1)+S_(j+1)=0. Taking the maximum absolute column sum gives mM≤2M and forces S=0 for the repaired range. The equation then says x_(a,j+2)=−x_(a,j), so the nonzero signs have least period exactly four. Conversely any two balanced named columns and their negatives close and satisfy all equations if four divides n. They give a bijection with the square of the set of balanced length-m columns, without quotienting rotations or colors; exchange has no fixed assignments. The contextual prism calculation is also exact: upper triples of a parity configuration must not be monochromatic, and in four-periodic blocks with two ones the lower row is a shift by two, so its triples satisfy the same test.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite family of graph products, the result classifies the complete sign solution set, not just existence or dimension of a linear space. It identifies exactly when closure is possible, all first-two-column choices, and the labelled and color-exchange-quotiented counts. The result remains useful after removal of the covered prism subcase; there is no claim of a general complexity result.
